content.prompt: Determine the equation for each logarithmic graph in the form $y=\log_a(x-b)+c$.

spec.description: Unfilled graph without a grid. Double-ended axes, numbered ticks, red dashed vertical asymptote, blue logarithmic curve and two blue points with black coordinate labels. Coordinate labels are above-left of their points.

answer.short:
$y=\log_2(x+3)$

Use the vertical asymptote for the horizontal shift, then substitute labelled points to find the base and vertical shift.
answer.worked:
The vertical asymptote is $x=-3$, so $b=-3$.
$$\begin{align*}1&=\log_a2+c\\3&=\log_a8+c\\2&=\log_a8-\log_a2\\2&=\log_a4\\a^2&=4\\a&=2\end{align*}$$
The base must be positive and different from $1$.
$$\begin{align*}1&=\log_22+c\\c&=0\\y&=\log_2(x+3)\end{align*}$$

answer.worked:
The vertical asymptote is $x=2$, so $b=2$.
Using $(3,3)$:
$$\begin{align*}3&=\log_a1+c\\c&=3\end{align*}$$
Using $(6,5)$:

$$y=\log_2(x-2)+3.$$
